keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the whole life. The pages name Zhen Prefecture (capital) and the Shen and Ji prefectures attacked by Later Liang in 910, and give no area; the 80 km circle at Shijiazhuang is the reading the former-jin dossier uses for the 922 gain. Shen and Ji (Hengshui) lie farther east and may lie outside the circle.

ledger.note: 763: the Chengde circuit stays with a Yan general. After the rebellion 'Yan generals who surrendered to Tang were allowed to remain as independent military governors'; Li Baozhen controlled Chengde Circuit, and 'Wang Rong, its last ruler, later founded the Zhao dynasty, which lasted until 921'. The page dates the settlement to 763; the circuit's extent is the researcher's reading.

883: Wang Rong succeeds at six. After his father Wang Jingchong died 'Wang Rong, only six-years-old' was supported by the Chengde soldiers as acting military governor; Xizong confirmed him and later that year made him full governor. In 900 he became Zhu Quanzhong's vassal and sent hostages.
907: the Chengde circuit becomes the Wushun and its governor Prince of Zhao. 'Zhu founded Later Liang. Chengde was renamed Wushun, Wang recognized Zhu, and Zhu made him Prince of Zhao.'

910: Wang Rong breaks with Later Liang. Later Liang's attacks on Shen and Ji prompted him to seek Jin's aid; 'Wushun and Yiwu broke with Later Liang, restored the Tang era name Tianyou, and became effectively independent'.
921: Wang Rong is murdered. In spring 921 his guard soldiers killed him during a Taoist ceremony; Wang Deming (Zhang Wenli) took control and submitted to Li Cunxu; Zhang Chujin succeeded his father.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks it); requested by the former-jin dossier under the slug zhao-five-dynasties-period (its 922 gain uses a Shijiazhuang 80 km disc) and by the Tang group's scope as one of the Hebei Three Circuits. One state for the Chengde circuit of 763-910 and the Zhao of 910-922 (the Wang family, the same capital), so the colour stays; the name keeps the slug other dossiers use. The pages opened give almost nothing on 763-883 (no dates for Li Baozhen, Li Weiyue, Wang Wujun or Wang Tingcou; the English Wikipedia has no Chengde Circuit article: Chengde_Circuit returned not found), so this stretch is a single keyframe. The 781-782 rebellion of the Hebei circuits and the 821-822 events are on the Weibo page only (see weibo-circuit). The Tang dossier carries the Hebei circuits only as 763 'Hebei, where surrendered Yan generals keep their posts'.
